# tawk — test coverage notes

**Status: FINALIZED at P1 (2026-09-24).** Suite `004`–`007` = **592 cases**,
green on bash 5.2.37 (primary, **GNU Awk 5.0.0**, Git for Windows'
`/usr/bin/gawk`) and on bash 5.3.9 (secondary, **GNU Awk 5.4.0**, msys64's), in
the default threaded mode and under `--mode single` (5.2.37). The per-file
counts below sum to 592 — 396 + 105 + 79 + 12 — and **every case in the suite
is covered by a row**.

**How the rows are cut.** Most of `004_Argv.sh` is generated by loops and small
helpers (`deny`, `denyb`, `setvar_bad`, `pass_extra`, `sbx`, `enc_case`, …) —
one helper call is one case. A family of such cases that asserts the same thing
over different words is ONE row here, with its case count in the ID and every
word listed, so the row count is smaller than the case count but no case is
unaccounted for: the counts in each heading are the sum of the counts in its
rows. Hand-written cases have a row of their own.

**Protocol.** `TAwk` has no FPC upstream: it is the sixth wrapper on
[`TUtil`](../tutil/README.md), itself a kcl addition
([../tutil/docs/TUtil.md](../tutil/docs/TUtil.md)). The oracle is **the bare GNU
tool on the same fixture**, run with the same arguments, never a second call
into the code under test. Decision **D4** pins the *dialect* — GNU Awk — not a
binary, and the two target bashes resolve two different versions (5.0.0 and
5.4.0) whose **message texts differ**, so gawk's own lines are matched by the
`gawk: ` prefix (the directory warning, identical on both, is pinned exactly)
and behaviour, not text, is what the cases pin. Every behavioural file opens
with the **GNU banner gate**: if `gawk --version` does not begin with `GNU Awk `,
every behavioural case is a loud SKIP and the case **count is unchanged**.
**Stdin is closed** for every behavioural file (`exec </dev/null`): gawk with
no program, or with a path it takes for the program, reads stdin and would
hang (the planning probe did).

The suite splits in two on purpose:

* **`004_Argv.sh` never executes gawk.** Every typed option is pinned by
  comparing the built array, which is what `argv NAME` exists for; it is the fast
  half and it is where the surface — and this unit's getopt-following deny-list —
  lives.
* **`005`/`006`/`007` run the tool** on a fixture tree chosen for the traps: a
  3-line `a 1`/`b 2`/`c 3` file and a 2-line second file, a CRLF file, a file
  ending in `\r\r\n`, a NUL-separated file with a CRLF **inside** a record and an
  unterminated last record, an unterminated last line, a `:`-separated and a
  TAB-separated file, two program files, a name with a space, a name starting
  with `-`, files literally named `k=v` and `a::b=v`, a directory, a marker
  directory and a `plant/` directory for the planted `inplace.awk`. In-place cases
  edit **copies** and assert the bytes with `od -c`; the sandbox cases prove
  "nothing ran / nothing was written" with **marker files**.

The Basis column cites one of:

* **A1–A13** — a pinned fact of [`PLAN.md`](PLAN.md) §3.
* **Q1–Q4** — an owner decision of [`PLAN.md`](PLAN.md) §2.0.
* **C1–C20** — a finding of the 2026-09-23 critic pass ([`PLAN.md`](PLAN.md) §8,
  same numbering). Every one of the twenty is cited by at least one row below,
  or named under "deliberate gaps".
* **Q6r** — review question 6 of P0 (2026-09-24,
  [`tawk_ledger.json`](tawk_ledger.json)): `backupSuffix` goes through the same
  encoder as `setVar`. Eight cases were added for it, six of them red against the
  pre-fix source.
* **P0-n** — a P0 implementation note recorded in the ledger: `switch`/`case`/
  `default` refused as `setVar` names like the §2.2 keywords (gawk's fatal rc 2 on
  both versions); `setVar` with other than two arguments is rc 2; `buildArgv`
  re-validates the names in `${inst}_vnames`; the directory warning text
  (`cmd. line:1:` and a backtick) as measured.
* **P3-F1** — the tgrep finding this unit inherits with its guard
  ([../tgrep/README.md §4](../tgrep/README.md)).
* **D4 / D6** — a decision: D4 the GNU dialect gate, D6 final `subshellOk`.
* **§n** — a section of [`PLAN.md`](PLAN.md) (or of [README.md](README.md)).

**Classes.**

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `contract` | the kcl contract ([../README.md](../README.md) §1): rc mapping, `RESULT`, silence, validation order, `set -eu` cleanliness, lifecycle, zero forks |
| `argv` | the typed option set → the pinned command line, asserted **without running gawk** |
| `tool-behaviour` | what GNU Awk 5.0.0 / 5.4.0 actually do, measured against the bare tool as oracle |
| `security` | the sandbox default (owner Q1), the deny-list's dangerous options, the planted include: what is refused, that it fails closed, that nothing ran |
| `representation` | paths, programs, variable values and records are **data**: a backslash, a newline, a leading `@`, a leading `-`, a CR, NUL framing, UTF-8, an unterminated tail |
| `boundary` | an edge the happy path never reaches: no program, no path, a missing file in the middle, nesting, a reused instance name |
| `perf` | a [`PLAN.md`](PLAN.md) §5 P1 gate, asserted with a loose ceiling |

**Where the registry cases live.** tawk appends `__taw_` to
`TUTIL_OUT_PREFIXES` and `_progs _vnames _vvals` to `TUTIL_OUT_SUFFIXES`; it did
not change tutil's code or tests. The registries' own cases — the reserved
names, the fail-closed empty / unset / scalar registry — are in
[`../tutil/tests/001_Core.sh` §C](../tutil/tests/001_Core.sh) (see
[../tutil/TEST_COVERAGE_NOTES.md](../tutil/TEST_COVERAGE_NOTES.md), the
`001.reg-*` rows). This file's rows cover the **tawk side**: the four names are
registered once, idempotently, and refused through a `TAwk` instance with the
instance's lists intact.

**Deliberate gaps** (each is stated in [`PLAN.md`](PLAN.md) and restated in
[README.md](README.md)):

* **BSD awk / mawk** (D4, PLAN §1.3) — nothing to assert on this box.
* **a callback's bare assignment** (**C19**) — a callback that assigns a bare
  `sandbox=0` or `program=` writes the instance's property through dynamic
  scoping; measured at planning, documented as a caller rule (README §4,
  "callbacks declare `local`"), not a wrapper behaviour.
* **the 5.4 sandbox refusing `ARGV[ARGC++]`** (**C5**, second half) and **the
  in-place traps not pinned** (**C13**: ENDFILE output goes into the file, a
  fatal runtime error leaves the file untouched) — gawk's own behaviour,
  measured by the critic, documented in README §4/§6; the wrapper does nothing
  with them. END-to-stdout and `exit`-truncates ARE pinned (005 §G).
* **`programFile` resolved through AWKPATH** (**C15**, first half) — documented
  as deviation (h); `programFile = -` (the second half) is pinned.
* **the env route** (**C16**) — moot since the critic pass; its absence is
  pinned by 006.0-ext-include.
* **an empty path operand `''`** — passed through for tool parity (gawk skips
  it, rc 0); documented in README §1, no case of its own.
* **gawk's own stderr** — the tool's `gawk: …` lines pass through by design and
  their text differs between the versions, so `005`/`006` count *our* lines and
  the tool's separately and match the tool's by **prefix** only.

---

## 004_Argv.sh — typed options to argv, nothing executed (P0) — 396 cases

**gawk is never started in this file.** Every case either compares the array
`a.argv GOT` handed over, or asserts a refusal. A refusal (`check_rc2`) asserts
**five** things at once: rc 2, `RESULT ''`, the caller's array **untouched**,
`${inst}_argv` **EMPTY** (no stale command line can run afterwards), and exactly
**one** `kk.debug` line starting `Error: TAwk.buildArgv:` and naming the reason.

### A. A3 lifecycle and both out-name registries (25)

| ID | Members | Case | Class | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 004.a-vars-present | Create | all 9 TAwk vars + 5 TUtil vars (incl. `subshellOk`) are present in `${inst}_data` right after `new` — none unbound under `set -u` | contract | **A3**, §2.1 |
| 004.a-defaults | Create | the documented defaults: `program` = argument 1, **`sandbox` 1**, the other flags `0`, strings `''`, `cmd` `gawk`, `_lastRc` `-1`, `subshellOk` 0 | contract | **A3**, **Q1** |
| 004.a-args-empty | Create | `${a}_args` is EMPTY after `TAwk.new a PROGRAM PATH` — the `inherited`-in-a-constructor trap would have made PROGRAM the command | contract | **A3**, §2.1 |
| 004.a-arrays | Create | `_paths` holds every argument after PROGRAM verbatim (a space, `-dash`, a NEWLINE, `-`), and `_progs`, `_vnames`, `_vvals` are EMPTY **indexed** arrays (`declare -a …=()`) | representation | **A3**, **C9** |
| 004.a-no-arg | Create | `TAwk.new a` with no argument: `program ''`, no path, no chunk, no variable, `cmd gawk` | boundary | **A3** |
| 004.a-reuse-clean | Create | a REUSED instance name starts clean — `program`, `fieldSep`, `sandbox` (back to 1), `inPlace`, `backupSuffix`, `programFile` and all four lists re-assigned (`.new` does NOT clear `_data`) | boundary | **A3**, §2.1 |
| 004.a-delete | Destroy | `delete` removes `_paths`, `_progs`, `_vnames`, `_vvals`, `_args`, `_argv` and `_data` | contract | **A3**, §2.1 |
| 004.a-argv-nothing | argv | `argv` RUNS NOTHING — with `cmd` pointed at a function that would touch a flag file, the flag stays absent and the 6-word argv is still built | contract | **A1**, §1.2 |
| 004.a-badout ×13 | argv, toArray | each of these out-names is rc 2, `RESULT ''`, one line naming it (*bad output array name*): `argv __taw_v`, `argv __taw_x`, `toArray __taw_a` (refused BEFORE anything runs), `argv aA_progs`, `toArray aA_progs` (the records would become the next program), `argv aA_vnames`, `toArray aA_vnames`, `argv aA_vvals`, `toArray aA_vvals`, `argv aA_paths`, `argv aA_args`, `argv TUTIL_OUT_SUFFIXES`, `argv TUTIL_OUT_PREFIXES` | contract | **A3**, §2.1 |
| 004.a-lists-intact | — | after every refusal above the chunk list, `_vnames`, `_vvals` and `program` are unchanged | contract | **A3** |
| 004.a-registries-once | *(load)* | both registries extended exactly once: prefixes `(__tu_ __tg_ __th_ __tt_ __taw_)`, suffixes `(_args _argv _paths _progs _vnames _vvals)` | contract | **A3**, §2.1 |
| 004.a-registries-idempotent | *(load)* | sourcing `tawk.sh` twice more appends NOTHING | contract | **A3**, §2.1 |
| 004.a-badout-recovers | argv | an ordinary out-name still fills after every refusal (`gawk --sandbox -v x=1 -v y=two -e {print} -e END{print NR} -e BEGIN{} -- f.txt`) | contract | **A3** |

| 004.b-inplace | `inPlace = 1` (sandbox 0) → `BINMODE=3`, then `-i /usr/share/awk/inplace.awk` — the ABSOLUTE include | **Q4**, **C6** |

| ID | Case | Class | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|

| 004.c-no-accumulate | rebuilding does not ACCUMULATE — two `argv` calls agree word for word | contract | **A1** |
| 004.c-argv-copy | `argv` hands over a COPY — writing it does not touch `${inst}_argv` | contract | **A1** |

in 005 §B).

## 005_Run.sh — TAwk against GNU Awk on a real tree (P0) — 105 cases

Oracle = the bare tool on the same fixture. Records are compared as arrays
(newline framed, the unterminated tail kept; NUL framed under `nullData`),
streams byte for byte with `cmp` or `od -c`. Every oracle and every child runs
with stdin closed and under `timeout 20`.

|---|---|---|---|
| 005.z-banner | the `gawk` on PATH is GNU Awk — otherwise every case below is a loud SKIP and the count is unchanged; the PASS line names the binary and its version | contract | **D4** |
| 005.z-fixture | the fixture tree is in place (a real `\r` in the CRLF file's bytes) | contract | §4 |

## 006_Contract.sh — the kcl contract for TAwk (P0) — 79 cases

### 0. source integrity (14)

Two earlier mechanical sweeps corrupted kcl sources while tests stayed green, so
this section reads the file itself. Class `contract` throughout.

| ID | Case | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| 006.0-parse | the unit source parses (`bash -n`) | §6 |
| 006.0-open-quote | no single-quoted `printf` format is left open at end of line | §6 |
| 006.0-inline-cr | no member body carries an inline `$'\r'` | §6 |
| 006.0-this | no internal member call is spelled `$this.NAME` | tutil PLAN §2.2 |
| 006.0-sentinel | the red-first skeleton sentinel `__TAWK_PENDING__` is GONE | §5 |
| 006.0-ctor | the CONSTRUCTOR calls `parent.constructor gawk`, never `inherited`, assigns `sandbox=1` and `program="${1:-}"`, and declares the four indexed arrays with `declare -ga` | §2.1, **Q1**, **C9** |
| 006.0-dtor | the DESTRUCTOR frees `_paths`, `_progs`, `_vnames`, `_vvals` with `unset -v`, then chains with `inherited` | §2.1 |
| 006.0-rc-preserving | the four overridden func sinks use the rc-PRESERVING spelling (guarded `inherited X "$@" \|\| …`, RESULT saved, rc re-raised, no body ENDS on `inherited`) | §2.5 (thead's blocker) |
| 006.0-each-proc | the overridden PROC `each` re-raises the rc and never answers RESULT | §2.5 |
| 006.0-no-bin-bookkeeping | the derived BINMODE lives in `buildArgv` only — no `binary=` in the builder, no `_binDerived` | §2.4 |
| 006.0-ext-include | the inplace extension is included only by its ABSOLUTE path, never `-i inplace`; no `ENVIRON` / `env` route | **C6**, **C16**, **Q2** |
| 006.0-no-shadow | no `var` shadows a TUtil or kklass member name, and there are exactly **9** of them | tutil PLAN §1.2 |
| 006.0-one-source | the unit sources ONLY `../tutil/tutil.sh` | §1.2 |
| 006.0-registered | `__taw_` and `_progs _vnames _vvals` registered at load, once each | §2.1 |

### Z. the banner gate (1)

| ID | Case | Class | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| 006.z-banner | the `gawk` on PATH is GNU Awk; otherwise every case that runs gawk is a loud SKIP | contract | **D4** |

### 1. `set -eu` — the instance, `a.each` and both TPipe forms (25)

Each `expect_clean` case runs its snippet in a **child** under `set -eu` (and
`timeout 60`, stdin `/dev/null`) with the unit freshly sourced, and asserts rc 0,
stdout exactly `OK`, and **empty stderr**; every sink call inside is guarded
`|| rc=$?`. Class `contract`, basis **A13** throughout.

| ID | Case |
|---|---|
| 006.1-load | the unit loads under `set -eu` |
| 006.1-load-twice | it loads TWICE (every re-source guard holds, the registry appends stay idempotent) |
| 006.1-each | `a.each`: an instance that delivers records — rc 0, 3 calls, `lastRc` 0 |
| 006.1-tpipe-argv | form 2: `TPipe.each CB -- "${argv[@]}"` with the argv TAwk built (6 words) |
| 006.1-tpipe-apply | form 2 with `TAwk.apply` as the producer command |
| 006.1-lastpipe | form 1: a REAL pipe under `shopt -s lastpipe`, from `apply` and from `a.run` (`NR==2` → 1 record) |
| 006.1-func-sinks | every func sink on an instance that delivers: `toArray` 3, `count` 3, `first` `1` |
| 006.1-tolist | `toList` into a kklass instance with an `.Add` — offered 3, stored 3 |
| 006.1-setvar-verbatim | `setVar` with a backslash, a newline and a leading `@` (built with `printf -v`, 6 bytes) arrives verbatim through `run` (**Q2**, **C8**) |
| 006.1-setvar-refused | a refused `setVar` (the builtin `length`) — rc 2, nothing stored, no abort (**C10**) |
| 006.1-gawk-error | a gawk ERROR (the only file missing, raw 2) — `each` rc 1, 0 callbacks, `lastRc` 2, the child survives |
| 006.1-fatal-middle | the FATAL missing file in the middle — rc 1, the earlier records KEPT (`RESULT` 3 == kept), `lastRc` 2 (**C7**) |
| 006.1-exit7 | a program's `exit 7` on line 3 — `count` rc 1 RESULT 2, `lastRc` 7, no abort |
| 006.1-refused-noprogram | a REFUSED build (no program) — rc 2 from `each` (0 callbacks) / `toArray` (array untouched, RESULT `''`) / `count` / `run`, `lastRc` still -1 |
| 006.1-inplace | in-place: every sink rc 2 with the file untouched, then `run` (sandbox 0) rc 0 edits it (`A 1 B 2 C 3`) |
| 006.1-inplace-sandbox | in-place with the DEFAULT sandbox — `run` rc 2, no abort, the file untouched (**Q4**) |
| 006.1-denied | a denied extra (`addArg -W sandbox`) — rc 2 from `toArray` / `count` / `run`, no abort (**C2**) |
| 006.1-cmd-empty | an EMPTY `cmd` — rc 2 from every runner, no abort |
| 006.1-apply-refused | `TAwk.apply` with no path, and with an empty PROGRAM — rc 2, no abort, nothing printed (**C1**) |
| 006.1-apply-sandbox | `TAwk.apply` refused by the sandbox (`system()`) — rc 1, no abort |
| 006.1-run-streams | `run` streams (`NR==2` → `b 2`) and the raw rc is readable afterwards |
| 006.1-delete-clean | `delete` on an instance that never ran leaves no `_paths` / `_progs` / `_vnames` / `_vvals` / `_args` |
| 006.1-subst-once | the `$( )` position: a func sink prints its value exactly ONCE (`count` 3, `first` `1`) |
| 006.1-d6 | **D6 final**: `subshellOk = 1` silences TPipe's subshell warning through TAwk, and without it the verbatim `Warning: TPipe.toArray: the array A2 is filled inside a subshell (BASH_SUBSHELL=1) — …` appears (basis **D6**) |
| 006.1-unguarded | an UNGUARDED sink call with rc 1 aborts a `set -eu` caller (nothing printed after it) while the guarded one reads rc 1 and carries on — the documented caller rule |

### 2. the debug switch — one line per rc 2 / gawk-error path, silence otherwise (39)

`check_one` asserts the rc, **exactly one** line of ours with the switch ON
(containing the named substring), the same rc and **zero** lines of ours with
the switch OFF (gawk's own lines are counted separately). `check_silent` asserts
**no** line of ours at all. Class `contract`, basis **A13** and §1.2 of the kcl
README.

| ID | Case | Extra basis |
|---|---|---|
| 006.2-noprogram ×3 | rc 2: no program, through `each`, `count` and `run` (every runner reports once, not twice) | **C1** |

## 007_Bench.sh — the PLAN §5 P1 performance gate (P1) — 12 cases

Class `perf` throughout (except the banner gate and the fork cases, class
`contract`). **Two sets of numbers on purpose**: [`../bench.sh`](bench.sh)
measures the real **1.5×** gate by hand on an idle box from the medians of 21
interleaved runs (README §10); this file asserts the same shapes with a **10×**
ceiling, because ktests runs test files threaded (8 workers) and the two sides
of the ratio do not inflate together — `gawk` is its own process while the
wrapper's share is bash work in the contended shell. The clock is
`TStopwatch.getTimeStamp`; `date +%s%N` is forbidden (~20 ms per call on msys,
paid twice per sample — tfind PLAN §8 finding 17). Stdin is closed for the
whole file; the corpus comes from `kt_fixture_tmpdir_create`; the file installs
no `EXIT` trap of its own.

| ID | Case | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| 007.z-banner | the `gawk` on PATH is GNU Awk — otherwise every timed case is a loud SKIP, count unchanged | **D4** |
| 007.a-gate-big | `TAwk.apply '{print $2}'` over a 200-line file costs at most **10×** a bare `gawk --sandbox -e '{print $2}' --`, from the MEDIANS of 7 INTERLEAVED runs, with both sides' outputs asserted byte-identical (200 records) | §5 P1 |
| 007.a-gate-one | the same over a **ONE-line** file — the shape that shows corpus size is not the knob | §5 P1 |
| 007.a-delta | the `apply` delta IS one instance: `new PROGRAM` + `sandbox =` + `buildArgv` + `delete` (fresh names, as `apply` uses) under 50 ms/call (~4.7 ms idle; nine properties, four arrays), with the argv asserted | §5 P1 |
| 007.b-argv-nothing | 200 `buildArgv`/`argv` calls invoke the `cmd` **zero** times, never fork (`$BASHPID`), and build the 11 words in the pinned order (`--sandbox --lint -v lim=5 -e … -e END{print NR} -- FILE`) | **A1**, §5 P1 |
| 007.b-argv-constant | the build stays constant-cost: 201 rebuilds do not accumulate words | **A1** |
| 007.b-refused-cheap | a REFUSED build is the cheap path too: 100 deny-list rc 2 calls (`-Wsandbox` after `-n --lint`, so the whole scan and the `-W` table run) invoke the `cmd` zero times, fork nothing, and leave `${inst}_argv` empty | **A2**, **C2** |
| 007.b-enc-1k | the `setVar` ENCODING of a 1 KiB value (backslashes, newlines, a leading `@`) is fork-free and under 20 ms per build (~1.9 ms idle): the `-v` word is exactly 2 + 1219 bytes starting `x=\100`, the stored value still verbatim | **A5**, **C8**, §2.3 |
| 007.c-count | `a.count` over 200 records costs at most 10× `gawk … \| wc -l` — published, **not** the gate; both count 200 | §5 P1 |
| 007.d-sinks-fork | the five sinks: the callback and `.Add` run in THIS process, one record each (`first` = `xyz`) | **A13** |
| 007.d-members-fork | the ONLY fork per call is gawk: eight property writes, ten builder members (`paths`, `addProgram`, `clearPrograms`, `setVar`, `clearVars`, `addArg`, `clearArgs`, `buildArgv`, `argv`, `mapRc` twice — 2 → 1, 7 → 1), `lastRc`, `run` and `apply` leave `$BASHPID` untouched | **A13**, **Q3** |
| 007.d-refused-fork | the rc 2 paths fork nothing: a deny-list hit (`--so=x`), an in-place sink, a path-less and an empty-program `apply`, an illegal `setVar` name (`ENVIRON`) — all rc 2, `lastRc` still -1 | **A2**, **Q4**, **C1**, **C10** |
